subject: Logic
title: Cantor's Diagonal Argument
description: Learn Cantor's Diagonal Argument in one minute.

hook.text: Some infinities are bigger than others. If that sentence hurts your brain, Georg Cantor felt the same way in 1891.

buildup.text: Cantor asked: can you list all real numbers between 0 and 1? Assume you can—number them in a list.

discovery.text: Now build a new number: change the first digit of entry 1, the second digit of entry 2, and so on diagonally.

twist.text: This new number differs from every entry on the list—so it can't be on the list. The list can never be complete.

climax.text: The real numbers are uncountably infinite—a bigger infinity than the counting numbers. Infinity has levels.

punchline.text: Not all infinities are the same size.

quiz.question: What did Cantor's diagonal argument prove?
options: The real numbers are a bigger infinity than the natural numbers
